observation_summary: The JsonParserSequence was incorrectly skipping tokens when switching between concatenated parsers, causing the parser to return the wrong token value (e.g., 3 instead of 2).
hypothesis: The JsonParserSequence implementation of nextToken() was unconditionally calling nextToken() on the delegate parser upon switching, which caused it to skip the current token if the parser was already initialized at a valid token position.
prediction: The fix will involve adding state tracking (like _suppressNextToken) to determine if the current token has already been consumed or is already available, and adjusting the nextToken() logic to return the current token instead of advancing if it is already set.
experiment_rationale: The diff shows the introduction of a boolean flag _suppressNextToken and a modification to the nextToken() method to check this flag and return the current token if set, rather than unconditionally calling delegate.nextToken(). This confirms the logic for token advancement was flawed.
reasoning_summary: The defect is in the procedural logic of the nextToken() method, which failed to correctly handle the state of the delegate parser when switching. It was unconditionally advancing the parser, which is an algorithmic error in the sequence traversal logic. It is not a missing check (Checking) because the logic itself was fundamentally flawed in its iteration strategy, nor is it a simple initialization error.
evidence_used: The diff shows the addition of _suppressNextToken to track state.
The diff shows the modification of nextToken() to return delegate.currentToken() if _suppressNextToken is true.
The diff shows the modification of the loop logic to check delegate.hasCurrentToken() before calling delegate.nextToken().

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a check for the flag, the root cause is the incorrect iteration strategy (advancing when it shouldn't) rather than a missing validation of input data.
The fix involves more than just setting a value; it requires a fundamental change to the procedural logic of how tokens are retrieved and advanced.
